legend: Gunga just learned what a double-ended queue is in his data structure class. a double-ended queue (deque) is an abstract data type that generalizes a queue, for which elements can be added to or removed from either the front (head) or back (tail).

Now, he is playing with his own double-ended queue. He has an empty double-ended queue B%%ZSMJ0%% and an array of integers A%%ZSMJ1%%. In the i%%ZSMJ2%%-th move, he will add Ai%%ZSMJ3%% to one end of B%%ZSMJ4%%. His goal is to maximize the sum of values from BL%%ZSMJ5%% to BR%%ZSMJ6%%, inclusively. Bi%%ZSMJ7%% is defined as the i%%ZSMJ8%%-th element in the deque from the front.
Formally, find the maximum value over all possible B%%ZSMJ9%% formed in the end:
input: The first line contains an integer n,L,R%%ZSMJ11%% (1≤n≤2×105,1≤L≤R≤n)%%ZSMJ12%% – the number of integers and Gunga's favorite interval.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ13%% space-separated integers A1,A2,…,An%%ZSMJ14%% (−109≤Ai≤109)%%ZSMJ15%%.
output: Output the maximum sum from BL%%ZSMJ16%% to BR%%ZSMJ17%%.
